Manuel Ríos Ruiz concluye que no se sabe con certeza. La Niña de los Peines se hizo inmortal con su copla «Péinate tú con mis peines». Del tango nacen los tientos, más pausados y solemnes, que cantaron primero el Mellizo y el Marrurro y se popularizaron a comienzos del XX, y la mariana, que difundió Bernardo el de los Lobitos y hoy casi solo canta Pepe Menese con letras de Moreno Galván.

scenes.name: Las soleares
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: La madre del cante y uno de sus pilares, independiente de cualquier otro ritmo; los cantaores la consideran «el toro bravo del arte jondo». Coplas solemnes y sentenciosas de tres o cuatro octosílabos, unidas por la guitarra, que suelen rematarse por bulerías; muy apropiadas para el baile de mujer. Se desarrolló al sur del Guadalquivir desde los jaleos festivos: la primera mención es de la Andonda en Triana hacia 1840, una cantaora temible contemporánea del Fillo, y tomó su forma actual entre 1875 y 1915. Las mujeres fueron clave en su creación y transmisión (la Andonda, Mercedes la Serneta, Fernanda de Utrera, Carmen Linares). Hay soleares de Triana (la Andonda, Silverio, Fernando el de Triana, la Niña de los Peines, Tomás Pavón, Mairena), de Alcalá, más solemnes (Joaquín el de la Paula, Juan Talega), de Utrera (la Serneta, el Pinini, María Peña, Fernanda), de Cádiz y el Puerto, más jondas (Enrique Butrón, el Mellizo, Paquirri el Guanté), de Jerez, breves y llenas de melismas (Curro Frijones, José Illanda, Juan Mojama, Tío José de Paula, Manuel Torre) y de Córdoba, más pausadas.

scenes.name: Las siguiriyas, livianas y serranas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Una de las expresiones más dramáticas y de los palos más importantes: sin siguiriyas y soleares el flamenco no sería lo que es. Un quejío entero de lamentos que no admite medias tintas («con las siguiriyas no se puede vender la burra»), con coplas trágicas de cuatro versos (6, 6, 10 y 6 sílabas), muchas sobre la muerte de los seres queridos, y falsetas lentas que suenan a campanas a muerto. Lorca la describió como un grito terrible que divide el paisaje en dos; Tía Anica la Piriñaca decía que cuando la cantaba a gusto la boca le sabía a sangre. La cantaban ya el Planeta (la de la Luna, la más antigua conocida) y el Fillo; luego Manuel Torre, Silverio, Paco la Luz, Cagancho, el Nitri, Curro Dulce, el Loco Mateo, el Mellizo, Terremoto de Jerez (que cantó toda la noche por siguiriyas con su madre muerta en brazos) y Juan Talega; hoy el Chocolate y José Menese. Antonio Mairena grabó unas cuarenta y cinco formas: es el siguiriyero más importante. Sus escuelas son Jerez y los Puertos, Cádiz y Triana. En el baile la difundió Vicente Escudero y Pilar López le añadió los palillos. La liviana, cante de campo, caminos y bandoleros, prepara la voz para la serrana, a la que Silverio dio brillo y con la que se remata por siguiriyas.

scenes.name: La caña, el polo y la petenera
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Tres cantes de la familia de la soleá. La caña, con ayes más arrastrados, se sitúa en la serranía de Ronda (un viajero inglés la oyó allí en 1830) o en la voz árabe gaunia, «canción»; la cantaron el Fillo, Tío José el Granaíno, Antonio Chacón, Pepe de la Matrona y Rafael Romero el Gallina, y hoy se usa más para el baile solemne. El polo se cantaba tras la caña, con la misma métrica; el de Tobalo, su supuesto creador, aparece ya en Estébanez Calderón y hoy se usa en la soleá apolá; Enrique Morente grabó el de Chacón. La petenera, melancólica y de origen incierto, se atribuye a una mujer de Paterna de la Ribera, «la perdición de los hombres», o a los sefardíes de los Balcanes; los gitanos la evitaron porque traía mala suerte. La cantaron la Niña de los Peines, Naranjito de Triana, Rafael Romero, Fosforito y hoy Pepe Menese.

scenes.name: Los cantes de Málaga: malagueñas, rondeñas, jaberas y verdiales
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Después de Sevilla y Cádiz, Málaga es la provincia con más variedad de cantes. La malagueña, cante libre, sin medida y sin baile, de rico toque, ha influido en las granaínas y en todos los cantes minero-levantinos. Nació en Álora (las malagueñas perotas) a partir de los fandangos abandolaos, acompañados de bandola; tras los anónimos y los de Cipriano Pitana, Francisco Jiménez y Joaquín Tabaco, Juan Breva le dio identidad propia, y Lorca escribió de su trino. Su esplendor es la segunda mitad del XIX, con el Canario, la Trini, Baldomero Pacheco y Fosforito el Viejo; también firmaron malagueñas el Mellizo, único gitano creador de una (inspirada en el prefacio de la misa), y Chacón. Diego Clavel recogió treinta y una en los noventa. La rondeña, de principios del XIX y de la tierra del Tobalo, es la pieza con que muchos guitarristas abren sus conciertos; la jabera, ruda y difícil, debe su nombre a una vendedora de habas y está casi perdida; los verdiales, de probable raíz morisca, apenas han cambiado y conservan la panda con violín, panderos, chinchines y cañas para la fiesta de san Juan.

scenes.name: Los tanguillos de Cádiz
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Vinculados al carnaval de Cádiz, son el soporte de chirigotas, coros y murgas; cantados en grupo pierden su naturaleza flamenca, que es individual, aunque como baile la conservan. Hay constancia de los «tangos graciosos» del barrio de La Viña en 1779, en la tonadilla La anónima de Tomás Abril, y el tango americano o de negros terminó de formarlos. Letras jocosas y satíricas: «el chiste ingenuo y feliz enfrente de la tragedia jonda del quejío» (Emilio Jiménez Díaz). Aurelio y Pericón de Cádiz, Manuel Vargas y la Perla los grabaron en la primera mitad del siglo XX, y hasta Mairena dejó dos. Chano Lobato, su mayor cultor, los elevó a cante noble y recrea la venta de los cuadros que popularizó Pericón.

scenes.name: Las tonás: martinetes, carceleras y deblas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Cantes sin acompañamiento, prueba de su antigüedad, en cuartetas octosílabas de intensa carga dramática y origen gitano indiscutible: son crónicas de la miseria, la cárcel y la persecución. Demófilo ya las daba en 1881 por «cantes viejos casi caídos en desuso»; en el siglo XIX hubo entre veintisiete y treinta y cuatro, cada una con el nombre de su creador. La más antigua es la de Tío Luis el de la Juliana, aguador y primer cantaor del que hay noticia (segunda mitad del siglo XVIII), conservada por Antonio Chacón y recreada por Pepe de la Matrona; se le atribuye también la toná de los pajaritos, que recuerda la tonada sefardí de los bilbilicos. Los martinetes toman el nombre del martillo de la fragua, aunque es difícil cantar mientras se forja: Tío Juane de Jerez montaba una fragua en escena en los setenta y ochenta, y Antonio el Bailarín creó su baile con martillo y yunque; la familia fragüera más antigua es la de los Cantorales de Cádiz, que Silverio visitaba. Las carceleras cantan la prisión y servían para pasar mensajes en romaní desde las rejas. La debla, único palo con nombre romaní («diosa»), es religiosa, casi perdida y muy difícil; llegó a hoy por Tomás Pavón en los cuarenta y la recuperó Antonio Mairena.

scenes.name: Las sevillanas
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Nacen de las seguidillas castellanas, que en Sevilla se hicieron más vivas y fáciles de repetir: cuatro coplas para bailar en pareja un galanteo, con temas andaluces, amorosos o rocieros (corraleras, rocieras, bíblicas, de feria, marineras, romeras). Lorca recogió una del siglo XVIII. Su gran auge comercial llegó en los setenta, con millones de discos que daban envidia a los flamencos; las han grabado con jondura Manuel Vallejo, la Niña de los Peines, la Paquera de Jerez, el Turronero, Chiquetete y Camarón.

scenes.name: El fandango
scenes.book: El flamenco contado con sencillez
scenes.desc: Muy apreciado por su musicalidad y fácil de interpretar, no es un palo básico pero no es menor: la vieja división entre cantes grandes y chicos está obsoleta, y la jondura la pone el intérprete, no la antigüedad del palo. Canto para bailar de origen muy antiguo e incierto (Corominas lo deriva del portugués fado; hay quien le ve un lejano origen árabe), aparece por escrito en un entremés de 1705 y lo describe el deán Manuel Martí en 1712; en el siglo XIX fue el cante y baile nacional español, y a finales de siglo se aflamencó en Andalucía y dejó de bailarse. De él salen las granaínas, las malagueñas y los cantes de Levante, y hay fandangos propios en Lucena, Cabra, Puente Genil, Jaén, Granada o Almería. Su apogeo en la ópera flamenca lo desprestigió tanto que a cantaores como Pepe Menese les parece un insulto que se lo pidan; desde los años ochenta se revaloriza.

facts.title: Tin Machine as a Response to Art Punk (1989)
facts.body: Bowie formed Tin Machine as a deliberate move away from pop, submerging his identity into a "grungy rock band" with a metallic, feedback-laden sound. This was his direct response to the rising art punk sound of bands like Pixies and Sonic Youth, showcasing his commitment to noisier, more experimental rock. "It was his response to the rising art punk sound of bands like the Pixies or Sonic Youth."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Tin Machine Identity Struggle (1989-1992)
facts.body: Despite generating hits on the modern rock chart, Tin Machine never developed a personality beyond its status as "David Bowie's side project." The albums' poor sales, with the debut not even going gold, ultimately led Bowie back to his solo career. "While Tin Machine's workmen like Alt Rock proved decent radio fodder, the band never developed a personality beyond its status as David Bowie's side project."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: David Bowie

facts.title: Jason Everman – 30-Day Member of Nirvana (February–July 1989)
facts.body: When Kurt invited him to join as second guitarist for Nirvana's first major tour in February 1989, Everman had no fishing season to attend to and agreed. He made his debut on February 25, 1989, at the University of Washington. He was present when British journalists flew in to cover the Seattle scene, and when *Bleach* (which he'd financed) was released on June 15. His final show was at the Pyramid Club in New York City on July 18, 1989; the rest of the tour was canceled and the band drove 50 hours back to Seattle without speaking. He was let go or quit — either way it was fine with him. He subsequently joined Soundgarden and after that went on to become a Special Forces soldier. "The band deadheaded back home to Seattle. They were so pissed with Jason that they nearly left him in New York."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Jason Everman's Brief Stint (February-July 1989) – Financial Benefactor and Second Guitarist
facts.body: Jason Everman joined Nirvana as a second guitarist and toured behind their *Bleach* album, notably paying the recording fee for the album. However, his personality was not deemed a good fit for the band, and he was ejected from February to July of 1989. "What wasn't fake was his time playing in Nirvana for a few months. But his personality didn't prove to be a very good fit, and he was soon under the band."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Sub Pop Singles Club Release of Bleach (1989)
facts.body: Nirvana's "Bleach" was the very first release through the Sub Pop Singles Club, where subscribers received a random 7-inch single monthly. These copies were mailed out on November 1, 1989. The most sought-after version is one of 1,000 copies hand-numbered in red pen on the white center label, which can be worth around $10,000. An additional 200 unnumbered copies likely served as promo copies for radio stations and music magazines. Counterfeits exist, so collectors are advised to check the "dead wax" for the inscription "Why don't you trade those guitars for shovels?". "This was the very first release through the singles club. They were all mailed out on November 1, 1989."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Jason Everman – 30-Day Member of Nirvana (February–July 1989)
facts.body: When Kurt invited him to join as second guitarist for Nirvana's first major tour in February 1989, Everman had no fishing season to attend to and agreed. He made his debut on February 25, 1989, at the University of Washington. He was present when British journalists flew in to cover the Seattle scene, and when *Bleach* (which he'd financed) was released on June 15. His final show was at the Pyramid Club in New York City on July 18, 1989; the rest of the tour was canceled and the band drove 50 hours back to Seattle without speaking. He was let go or quit — either way it was fine with him. He subsequently joined Soundgarden and after that went on to become a Special Forces soldier. "The band deadheaded back home to Seattle. They were so pissed with Jason that they nearly left him in New York."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Nirvana

facts.title: Adam Clayton Drug Arrest (August 6, 1989) – Possession with Intent to Traffic
facts.body: Bassist Adam Clayton was arrested in the parking lot of the Blue Light pub in Glen Allen, Ireland, for possession of 19 grams of marijuana. He was charged with intent to traffic under Irish law and fined £25,000, which was donated to the Women's Aid Refugee Center. Thanks to the Probation of Offenders Act, no official criminal conviction was recorded, allowing U2's scheduled tour to begin on September 15. "Paid a £25,000 fine and donated it to the Women's Aid Refugee Center."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: U2

facts.title: Auspicious Grammy Debut (1989)
facts.body: Rap's presence at the Grammys began inauspiciously in 1989 with the introduction of the Best Rap Performance Grammy, which was not televised. This led DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince to boycott the ceremony, highlighting early tensions between the genre and the Academy. "Raps' presence at the Grammys began inauspiciously in 1989, when a best rap performance Grammy was introduced, and DJ Jazee Jeff and the Fresh Prince's novelty hit Parents Just Don't Understand took the inaugural prize."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: British Journalists' Early Excitement - Early 1989
facts.body: The first professional journalists to become excited about the Seattle grunge scene were British, not American. This started in early 1989. "Now, many people have forgotten that the first professional journalists to really get excited about the Seattle grunge scene were not American. They were British."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Early UK Popularity - 1989
facts.body: Grunge was "all the rage in the UK" in 1989, even while most of North America remained unaware of it, largely due to early coverage by British music papers like Melody Maker and NME. "The result was that while most of North America was still unaware of grunge, it was all the rage in the UK."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12
facts.name: Grunge

facts.title: Mainstream Jump Post-1989
facts.body: After 1989, particularly with the release of Nirvana's *Bleach* and later albums by Pearl Jam and Alice In Chains, the grunge movement transitioned from Sub Pop to Geffen and became widely known globally. "Justo después ya todo el movimiento granch, saldría de su pop a Giffen y la parte más andegranada un pura se quedaría en su pop."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan

facts.title: Violator Album Signing Riot (March 20, 1989)
facts.body: The day after "Violator" was released, 17,000 fans (more than 5,000 initially) turned up for an autograph session at a warehouse record store on Lossiannigabullavard in Los Angeles. The event quickly devolved into a riot due to inadequate security, leading to seven police units clearing the area after an hour, bricks and bottles flying, two neon signs destroyed, and 150 LAPD officers in riot gear being called in. "The band was so crazy that the next day, 17,000 people turned up at an autograph session at a Los Angeles record store and a riot broke out."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: Post-Riot Apology and US Tour (March 1989)
facts.body: Following the riot at their Los Angeles autograph session, Depeche Mode issued an apology, stating they left to prevent serious injuries to their fans. The band confirmed they would return for a US tour that summer, starting at the end of May and ending in August on the west coast. "Peche Mode issued an apology in the wake of all that, saying they'd chosen to leave after only an hour at the scene in order to ensure that none of their fans got seriously injured."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour
facts.name: Depeche Mode

facts.title: First Meeting with Courtney Love (1989)
facts.body: Kurt Cobain first encountered Courtney Love on January 21, 1989, when Nirvana was performing at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon. Their initial interaction involved Kurt "unceremoniously help[ing] himself to Courtney's picture of beer." Afterwards, Kurt reportedly told friends that Courtney "looked like Nancy Spungin," referring to Sid Vicious's former girlfriend. "Courtney Love first saw Kurt Cobain when Nirvana played a show at the Satiricon Club in Portland, Oregon. The day was January 21st, 1989."

facts.title: Discovery at CMJ Music Conference (1989)
facts.body: In 1989, The Tragically Hip gained a significant break after playing the CMJ Music Conference in New York. Their inclusion on a delegate CD, common for highlighted artists at the time, led to their discovery by Canadian record company representatives who heard the disc back in Toronto. "The hip played the CMJ music conference in New York. And as was common back in those days, the organizers distributed a CD featuring some highlighted artists to all the delegates. The hip were on that disc. And that's what the Canadian record people company heard."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: Deal Signed at Horseshoe Tavern (1989)
facts.body: Following their discovery at CMJ and subsequent discussions, The Tragically Hip secured a record deal after a particularly powerful live show at the Horseshoe Tavern on Queen Street in Toronto. "When everybody got back to Toronto, it was time to discuss a deal. And after one particularly powerful show at the Horseshoe Tavern on Queen Street, the deal was done."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: The Tragically Hip

facts.title: High Cost of Sample Clearances (1989)
facts.body: For their 1989 album *Paul's Boutique*, the Beastie Boys used samples from 105 different songs. They managed to clear all these samples under older rules, but still spent nearly $300,000 on the clearances, demonstrating the substantial financial commitment required for sample-heavy productions even under less stringent regulations. "Even so, they spent nearly $300,000 on sample clearances. No one has that kind of money to make such an album today."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Music vs Technology Over The Years
facts.name: The Beastie Boys

facts.title: Formation Origin - Pickup Basketball Game (1989)
facts.body: The band's genesis began in Seattle when Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament formed Love Company and sought a singer by circulating a demo. Jack Irons, a former Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, received a copy of this demo and passed it to Eddie Vedder, a surfer and night shift worker at a Chevron tank farm in San Diego, after a pickup basketball game in 1989. Eddie then wrote lyrics to three of the demo's five songs, dubbed them onto a new cassette, and sent it to Seattle, leading to his invitation to jam with the group and the formation of Pearl Jam. "This cassette passed out of a gym bag sometime in 1989 might have resulted in the most profitable pickup basketball game ever played."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 6
facts.name: Pearl Jam

facts.title: Significant Video Spending (1989-2002)
facts.body: Between 1989 and 2002, Madonna spent over $32 million on just three music videos, adjusting for inflation. This substantial investment underscored her commitment to high-production-value visuals and her status as a pop superstar who used videos as major cultural events. "Madonna spent over $32 million on just three videos between 1989 and 2002."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: "Like a Prayer" Video Controversy (1989)
facts.body: The music video for "Like a Prayer" sparked the "most controversy of any Madonna production to date" due to its combination of religious iconography (Stigmata, burning crosses) with sex featuring a Black Christ figure. This put Madonna back into the "Culture Wars" and led Pepsi to cancel a planned $5 million ad campaign, though Madonna was able to keep the money. "Its video also stirred up the most controversy of any Madonna production to date, as its mix of religious iconography from Stigmata to Burning Crosses, coupled with sex with a black Christ figure, put Madonna right back into the Culture Wars again."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Fastest Rising Hit Since Debut (1989)
facts.body: "Like a Prayer" soared to number one on the Hot 100 in just six weeks, making it her fastest rising hit since "Like a Virgin" in 1984, signaling that her imperial phase was clearly not over yet. "Like a prayer soared to No. 1 on the Hot 100 in just six weeks, her fastest rising hit since Like a Virgin in 1984, the start of her imperial phase."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Ahead of the House Music Curve (1989)
facts.body: Madonna was "ahead of the curve" with her remixed "Express Yourself," which, with its multi-million dollar music video, established a house beat on Top 40 radio. This occurred before a broader wave of house singles began crossing over on the pop charts later in 1989. "Yet again, Madonna was ahead of the curve, getting a house beat on top 40 radio ahead of a wave of house singles that would begin crossing over on the pop charts later in 89."

facts.title: "Cherish" as Post-Divorce Uplift (1989)
facts.body: Madonna wrote "Cherish" as a "wistful song to cheer herself up" following her divorce from Sean Penn, making it her most optimistic and openly romantic hit of that period. "A wistful song she wrote to cheer herself up after her divorce from Sean Penn."

facts.title: Second Wave and Modern Definition (1989)
facts.body: The second major wave of techno emerged around 1989, led by artists like Richie Hawtin and Underground Resistance. This wave sought to reclaim the genre's essential underground roots, developing the minimalist, rhythm-heavy, monotonous, and constant sound that largely defines techno as it is known today, often without melodic emphasis. "En 1989 aparece Ander Grand Resistans, una serie de DJs y productores de música techno que vienen después de los grandes creadores, que se dan cuenta de que las grandes multinacionales han cogido el espíritu underground de Detroit y lo han convertido en una fábrica de dinero, quieren retomar la esencia en derrándole de Detroit."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: La historia del TECHNO en DETROIT. Cómo la música salvó a una ciudad atrapada

facts.title: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever – April 1989, Munich, Near-Fatal Illness Misidentified by European Doctors
facts.body: In April 1989, during a European tour, Bill Berry collapsed on stage in Munich with a fever of 103°F, chills, muscle aches, severe headache, nausea, red eyes, and a characteristic rash spreading from his wrists and ankles. German doctors, uncertain of the cause, prescribed tetracycline — the only antibiotic effective against Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, a tick-borne illness virtually unknown in Europe that Berry had almost certainly contracted while gardening before the tour. Had the German doctors chosen penicillin (the standard first choice), Berry would have received no benefit and might have suffered organ failure, coma, and death. The correct diagnosis was only confirmed after his recovery. "It wasn't until later that it was determined that Bill had come down with something called Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: R.E.M.

facts.title: Bill Berry's Near-Fatal Tick Bite (May 1989)
facts.body: While R.E.M. was on tour in Germany in May 1989, supporting the "Green Album," drummer Bill Berry fell severely ill shortly after arriving in Munich. Initially suspected to be bronchitis or measles due to a rash, his condition worsened with hallucinations and fluctuating consciousness. Despite doctors' panic and a "huge buffet of antibiotics," the cause remained unknown until one doctor's blind prescription of tetracycline proved effective. Bill's doctor in Athens, Georgia, later diagnosed Rocky Mountain spotted fever, which Bill had contracted from a tick bite while gardening at home a week prior, and whose week-long incubation period had led to symptoms emerging during the tour. "Bill varies near fatal bug bites"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 7
facts.name: R.E.M.

facts.title: Early History and Manchester Association - 1989
facts.body: Blur first appeared around 1989, originating from Colchester, East of London. Despite their geographic origin, they were often mistakenly associated with the Manchester scene due to their early sound, which featured "Manchester-ish bits" in songs from around 1991. "They had first serviced back in 1989 and although they were from Cold Chester, which is East of London, they were lumped into what was happening in Manchester in the Northwest, some 300 kilometers away."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

facts.title: Early Red Hot Chili Peppers Dynamics and Drug Use (1989-1991)
facts.body: Upon joining the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Frusciante initially bonded closely with Anthony Kiedis, but their relationship became problematic as Kiedis sought sobriety while Frusciante, a teenager, embraced a wild lifestyle of drinking and drugs, believing it was part of being a "Chili Pepper." He also felt immense pressure to fill Hillel Slovak's shoes. Despite his desire to get high, Frusciante's unique, melodic, "sinewy, slinky, slippery" style of playing was pivotal in transforming the band's sound, making Anthony more comfortable than he had been with Slovak, and influencing Flea's bass playing to become more melodic. "John was this teenager who wanted to drink and do drugs and have sex 24-7. He thought this was how you were supposed to be a Chili Pepper, wild and wacky, in his words."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1
facts.name: John Frusciante

facts.title: The Miracle (1989) - Album Cover Technology
facts.body: Although "The Miracle" is not always considered the most critically acclaimed album in Queen's career, its cover features a highly interesting graphic element: a single image blending the four faces of the band members. Created in 1989, this computer-generated composite was a technological marvel for its time, executed using the famous Quantel Paintbox, a precursor to Photoshop and other video editing programs. At the time, this advanced photographic editing technique was revolutionary, even if it seems unremarkable today. "Este dibujo que mezcla en una sola imagen las cuatro caras de los miembros de Queen es uno de los momentos interesantes desde el punto de vista gráfico y estamos hablando en 1989 y hacer esta especie de montajes fotográficos no era sencillo."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: QUEEN como iconografía estética y gráfica
facts.name: Queen

facts.title: Creative Breakthrough with Jim Sonefeld (1989)
facts.body: The band experienced a major creative breakthrough in the fall of 1989 when original drummer Brantley Smith left to pursue Christian ministry. He was replaced by Jim Sonefeld, a slightly older U of S.C. graduate who had played in goth-rock and classic rock bands and, crucially, was a budding songwriter. Sonefeld brought with him the song "Hold My Hand," which became a pivotal hit for the band. "The band's major creative breakthrough came in the fall of 1989, when original drummer Brantley Smith, uninterested in life on the road, amicably left the band to pursue Christian ministry. He was replaced by Jim Sony Sonafeld."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: Bowie's "Roots" Return (1989)
facts.body: The band was marketed as David Bowie returning to his roots as the frontman of a small rock combo, akin to his earlier days leading bands like the Manish Boys or the Lower Third. This was a deliberate move to submerge his pop identity into a grungy rock sound. "The band was billed as Bowie returning to his roots as the frontman of a small rock combo, like his 60s days leading the Manish Boys or the lower third."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Tin Machine

facts.title: Failure to Develop Identity (1989-1992)
facts.body: Despite proving decent radio fodder, Tin Machine never developed a personality beyond its status as "David Bowie's side project." This, coupled with poor album sales (their debut didn't even go gold, and "Tin Machine II" reached a meager number 126), ultimately led Bowie to return to his solo career after a three-year experiment. "While Tin Machine's workmen like Alt Rock proved decent radio fodder, the band never developed a personality beyond its status as David Bowie's side project."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.name: Tin Machine

facts.title: Courtney Love's First Husband – Punk Transvestite Singer Falling James Moreland (1989)
facts.body: Before marrying Kurt Cobain, Courtney Love had a drunken impulse-wedding in Las Vegas in 1989 with punk transvestite singer Falling James Moreland, the lead vocalist of the Leaving Trains (who had released albums on Black Flag's SST label). Moreland was the boyfriend of Jennifer Finch, who was about to join LA band L7. After sobering up, Courtney realized the mistake and they divorced within months. Moreland produced the first single for Courtney's new band, which was supposed to be called "Sweet Baby Crystal Powered by God" but was released as Hole — and the single was called "Retard Girl." "Listen, they've seen stranger things in Vegas."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Hole

facts.title: Financial State in 1989
facts.body: In 1989, when Nirvana recorded their debut album "Bleach," Sub Pop Records out of Seattle was described as "perpetually broke." "The band was a completely non-entity at the time, recording for the perpetually broke subpop records out of Seattle."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Sub Pop Records

facts.title: Singles Club (1989)
facts.body: In 1989, Sub Pop Records ran a "Singles Club" that mailed subscribers a random 7-inch single every month. The very first release through this club was Nirvana's "Bleach" single, mailed out on November 1, 1989, with 1,000 copies hand-numbered in red pen on the white center label, becoming highly valuable collectibles. "This was a club where the label mailed you a seven inch single every month, a random seven inch single."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Hype Strategy for Grunge Bands - Early 1989
facts.body: In early 1989, co-owners Jonathan Poe and Bruce Pabbitt, desperate to hype their acts like Nirvana, decided to emulate Jimi Hendrix's path to success by breaking bands in the UK first. Despite having no money, they risked flying a Melody Maker writer to Seattle to generate British press. "the two owners of the Subpop record label Jonathan Poe and Men and Bruce Pabbitt were desperate to hype their acts."

facts.title: Bristol Hip Hop Association (80s-1989)
facts.body: The Wild Bunch was a small association in Bristol active during the 1980s, including 1989. It served as a hub where many young, almost adolescent individuals gathered around hip hop culture, encompassing graffiti artists, DJs, singers, and breakdancers. This collective is credited with giving birth to the foundational bases of Trip Hop. "The Wild Bunch venía a ser una asociación dentro del Bristol que muchos jóvenes, casi adolescentes tenían en torno a la cultura hip hop."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan

facts.title: Recorded for $606.17, Paid for by Jason Everman
facts.body: Recorded in 1988 for a total cost of $606.17. Kurt Cobain didn't have the money, so his friend Jason Everman, a commercial fisherman from Alaska, paid the bill. As a thank-you, Everman was credited in the liner notes as having played guitar, even though he played no notes on the recording. "Kurt made it look like Jason played on the record, but let's be clear, he did not."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Bleach

facts.title: Recording Fee Paid by Jason Everman
facts.body: The recording fee for Nirvana's debut album *Bleach* was $606.17, which was paid to Jack Endino at Reciprocal Recording by Jason Everman. Everman, who briefly served as Nirvana's second guitarist, was given fake credit on the album for his financial generosity, although he did not play on the record. "He never played on the album, but was given fake credit on the record for his financial generosity."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: Bleach

The album's release on Sub Pop helped further solidify the grunge movement before its eventual leap to Geffen. "en el 89 se aliaba el lich el primer disco en Irvana también en su pop."

facts.body: The band's debut record, released on June 15, 1989, by the "perpetually broke" Sub Pop Records out of Seattle. Only 1,000 copies of the original vinyl version were pressed on white vinyl. A mint condition copy of this initial pressing can fetch as much as $5,500 today. "On June 15, 1989, the first Nirvana record came out. It was called Bleach."

facts.body: This album, released in 1989, is today considered a classic of Alt Rock. At the time, the band struggled to find an American label to release it, so they went through the British label 4AD, which specialized in experimental and avant-garde post-punk. "Back then, they couldn't find anyone in America to release it so they had to go through 4AD, the British label which specialized in experimental and avant-garde post-punk."

facts.title: Lawsuit by The Turtles (1989)
facts.body: In 1989, De La Soul faced a $1.7 million lawsuit from The Turtles for "stealing" a portion of their 1969 song "You Showed Me" for the track "Transmitting Why From Mars" on the album *3 Feet High and Rising*. The lawsuit was settled out of court, establishing a precedent against unauthorized sampling. "That resulted in a $1.7 million lawsuit against Dela Sol and their record company. Settled off court, but the message was clear. Do not sample without permission."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Music vs Technology Over The Years
facts.name: De La Soul

facts.title: a-ha and Norway's Electric Vehicle Revolution – Civil Disobedience Starting 1989
facts.body: In 1989, Morten Harket and Mags of a-ha joined former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland in driving an illegally non-toll-paying electric Fiat Panda (imported from Italy, backseat filled with batteries, 25-mile range, 20 hours to charge) around Norway, refusing to pay tolls, taxes, or parking fees, insisting that non-polluting vehicles should be exempt. They were fined repeatedly, declined to pay, and when the car was impounded and auctioned, they bought it back — 14 times. When Brundtland was re-elected Prime Minister in 1990, she made electrification of Norway's car fleet a government priority. By the 2020s, Norway has more electric vehicles per capita than any country on earth, with 90% of all new cars sold being electric. "It would not have happened without the help of a-ha."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.name: a‐ha
